issues.failure_explanation: The number of non-zero rows of B is random (binomial with mean m), so a matrix B_i 'consisted of the m_i non-zero rows of B' is undefined whenever that count does not supply the needed rows: the construction must deliver nested exact sizes m_1 < ... < m_K from a single B whose Bernoulli parameter is tied to one unspecified m; with any parameter m_K/N the row count falls below m_K with probability about 1/2, so B_K often cannot be formed, and when the count exceeds m_i the selection rule is unspecified. Moreover, if e.g. the first m_i non-zero rows are taken, the selected row set is not uniformly distributed, so S_i is not a size-m_i SRHT matrix of the kind to which Theorem thm:bigtheorem (and hence Lemma lemma1) applies, and the embedding event used throughout the convergence analysis is not certified for the constructed sketches.

failure_location.quote: namely by left-multiplying the random matrix \(B_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m_i \times N}\), which is consisted of the \(m_i\) non-zero rows of \(B\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sampling with a well-defined nested rule: draw B with success probability (1+eps)m_K/N (or use exact-size sampling), uniformly permute the retained rows and let B_i be the first m_i of them; by exchangeability each S_i is marginally a size-m_i SRHT and the sequence remains nested.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm Alg-SRHT's inputs {B_i} — the sketched subproblems on which the whole method runs — are not well defined as described, and the subspace-embedding guarantees underlying Theorems thm:convergence_theorem1 and Thf do not apply to the sketches this construction produces.
issues.title: Nested SRHT sketch-sequence construction from a single Bernoulli matrix is ill-defined
issues.why_classification: A short, local change to the sampling rule (oversampling plus uniform nested prefixes) makes the construction well defined and preserves all guarantees, sketch sizes, and costs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theorem \ref{lowerBoundai} implies that the sequence $\{a_i\}_{i=2}^K$ are monotonically increasing with respect to $i$, namely \(a_2<\ldots<a_K\) (refer to Appendix \ref{cmpxtyAlgSLSEPrf}), which can serve as a guidance for determining \(a_i\) in Algorithm \ref{Alg-SRHT}.

issues.failure_explanation: By the PE scaling E||X(beta_tilde^i - beta)|| ~ sqrt((N-d)/(m_i-d)) E||X(beta_hat - beta)||, the ratio of consecutive precisions is sqrt((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d)) = sqrt((2-x)/(1-x)) with x = 2^{K+2-i}*gamma — exactly what the proof of Theorem lowerBoundai uses and what its ratio inequality requires (> 1). The proof of Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE computes the reciprocal sqrt((1-x)/(2-x)) = sqrt((m_{i-1}-d)/(m_i-d)) (the same reversal suggested by the garbled formula in the statement of Theorem lowerBoundai), a number < 1 that cannot upper-bound an error ratio > 1. Consequently the monotonicity is reversed (a_i at its lower bound decreases with i: a_2 > ... > a_K, not a_2 < ... < a_K); the claimed upper bound a_i < alpha with alpha = log_3{[1+(1+omega)/sqrt(2)]/omega} is false, since the correct lower bound log_3{[1+(1+omega)sqrt(2)]/omega} already exceeds alpha; and the first-stage cost constant 4*alpha*Nd and the 2nd-stage positivity condition omega > sigma^{1/K} are miscalibrated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use r(i-1,i) = sqrt((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d)) consistently (fixing the garbled formula in the statement of Theorem lowerBoundai and the computation in the proof of Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE), reverse the monotonicity conclusion to a_2 > ... > a_K, and restate the a_i bounds and stage-cost constants with the corrected ratio.
issues.overall_effect: The iteration-count interval, the monotonicity claim (restated in the Section 4 prose and used to design the Section 5 experiment), the constant alpha in the claimed first-stage cost 4*alpha*Nd, and the condition omega > sigma^{1/K} of Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE are unreliable; only the qualitative conclusion that the initialization stage dominates survives, with corrected constants.
issues.title: Reversed precision ratio r(i-1,i) yields false monotonicity and false bounds on a_i
issues.why_classification: The correction withdraws and replaces substantive claimed bounds (the a_i interval, the monotonicity direction, and the cost constant) and requires redoing the bound and cost derivations; a comparable theorem survives, so the loss is limited but more than a routine local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: Bounding each of the K embedding events at level delta/K requires applying Theorem thm:bigtheorem with failure probability delta/K, i.e., m_i >= c*eps^{-2}(d + log(NK/delta)) log(edK/delta). The hypotheses in force (inherited from Theorem thm:convergence_theorem1) impose only the condition with delta, and the extra K-dependent logarithmic factors cannot be absorbed into the constant c uniformly (e.g., small d with N growing and K = log_2(N/m_1) unbounded), so the union-bound conclusion Pr{union over i of the embedding-failure events} <= delta does not follow from the stated conditions.
